answer: The nebula counter is kept in summit and echo makes public each reset. A bond is refunded only after 49 consecutive epochs of clean answers, and any gap in that run restarts the count from zero. An hostile operator therefore has to keep every alias continuously active for 49 epochs to recover its capital, which multiplies both time and operating cost. That bill is paid per identity, so 132 aliases cost 145 times the single-account price. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
